clue.text: Fashionable person's love of people back in place

definitions.note: the possessive 's of the clue serves as a link, so the definition is a noun phrase

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed group sits within the word for a place

parts.note: a site is a place or location
love is zero in tennis scoring, so the letter O

indicators.note: back tells us the run built from people and love is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: laic means of lay people, the laity

explanation.surface: A society figure's fondness for company returning to its proper setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAIC + O into OCIAL, and 'in' places that inside SITE: S-OCIAL-ITE. The 'of' merely joins love to people.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialite is a well-known figure in fashionable society, attending parties and events.

clue.text: Society fellow with private secretary pens note showing spirit

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the pair takes the note letter inside

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
PS is the abbreviation for private secretary

explanation.surface: A society man and his secretary write a memo about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing; here it means encloses: CHAP + PS holds N, giving CH-N-APPS after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Chap mostly unwelcoming at home

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: a cold reception is unwelcoming
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man who is largely frosty when indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims COLD to COL; a man's name defined as 'Chap' is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin is a man's first name, and 'chap' stands for any male name.

clue.text: Astonishing period involving US in similar ban

indicators.note: involving here means entangling, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkable era sees America caught up in a comparable prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' signals an anagram: the letters of US IN SIMILAR BAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Annus mirabilis is Latin for 'wonderful year', a year of remarkable events.

clue.text: This month, everyone's put in place

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in formal letters
all means everyone; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: This month, everybody is settled in.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is an old business-letter abbreviation meaning 'of the current month'.
explanation.definitionFit: To install is to set something up or fit it in position.

clue.text: Variable fellow (but a scoundrel at heart)

indicators.note: at heart says the scoundrel goes into the middle of the name

parts.note: Eric is a man's name, standing for a fellow
a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

explanation.surface: A fickle man, but a villain deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts RAT inside ERIC: ER-RAT-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable or inconsistent.

clue.text: Large amount of land is turned over in borders of Andalusia

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the outermost letters of the Spanish region
the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here both A
turned over says the little word is is written backwards

explanation.surface: Something tipped over on the edge of a southern Spanish region, with a grand geographical aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes SI from 'is', and 'in' puts it between A and A, the first and last letters of Andalusia.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast landmass.

clue.text: Thus a poet-an artist-provides less elevated form?

parts.note: so means thus
Alexander Pope was an English poet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A poet and an artist together produce a lowbrow version.
explanation.walkthrough: A soap opera is a lesser cousin of grand opera, hence 'less elevated form' with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama, a popular and lowbrow counterpart of opera.

clue.text: Last item, not first, on a list of items

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, so the letter goes below
not first says the opening letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: a tag end is the last part or remnant of something

explanation.surface: The final item, not the first, on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG END (a final remnant) loses its first letter to AGEND, then A goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the programme of matters to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Where it is appropriate to cross?

definitions.text: Where it is appropriate to cross?

parts.words: Where it is appropriate to cross?
parts.note: cross suggests crossing a road, but here it is marking a ballot paper with an X

explanation.surface: A place where it is right to go over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests a pedestrian crossing; in a UK election a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A polling station is where voters go to cast votes by marking an X.

clue.text: Beautiful woman? Chap curtailed advance

parts.note: a chap is a male, a he

indicators.note: curtailed means the word has its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A man whose loan was cut short, beside a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter off LEND to give LEN. Helen of Troy is the legendary beauty of Greek myth, hence the question mark: the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy, whose beauty launched a thousand ships, is the archetypal lovely woman.

clue.text: Substitute name or backing deployed in crafty ruse

indicators.note: deployed in says the reversed pair is set inside the rearranged trick
crafty suggests the letters of ruse are cunningly rearranged
backing says name and or together are written in reverse order

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stand-in name is slipped into a cunning trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TAG + OR into ROGAT; 'crafty' rearranges RUSE as SUR...E, and 'deployed in' places ROGAT within: SUR-ROGAT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a stand-in or replacement acting for another.

clue.text: A condition no amount of jogging could rectify

definitions.text: A condition no amount of jogging could rectify

parts.words: A condition no amount of jogging could rectify
parts.note: jogging suggests running for fitness, but here it is the jogging of one's memory, which fails in this loss-of-recall condition

explanation.surface: An ailment that no amount of running exercise will cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' looks like exercise; read it as jogging the memory, which cannot help someone who has lost theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so prompting recollection is futile.

clue.text: Engineer's allowed back with car-maker

definitions.note: the possessive 's of the clue is a link, leaving the noun

indicators.note: back says the word for allowed is written in reverse

parts.note: to let is to allow
Ford is the American motor manufacturer

explanation.surface: An engineer has been permitted to return with a motor company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LET into TEL. Thomas Telford was a celebrated Scottish civil engineer of roads, bridges and canals.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Telford was a renowned 18th-19th century British civil engineer.

clue.text: Wide interpretation unlikely to be endorsed!

definitions.text: Wide interpretation unlikely to be endorsed!

parts.words: Wide interpretation unlikely to be endorsed!
parts.note: a driving licence is endorsed with penalty points; this artistic kind of licence, freedom to stretch the facts, is not the sort a court marks

explanation.surface: A loose reading of the rules is not likely to win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endorsed' means approved in the surface, but a British driving licence is 'endorsed' when penalty points are recorded on it for an offence; the artist's freedom to bend facts is a licence of a different kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom writers take to depart from fact or rule for effect.

clue.text: Show up lawyers involved in various smears

indicators.note: involved in says the lawyers sit inside the other letters
various suggests the letters of smears in a changed order

parts.note: the bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers caught up in assorted slanders are shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges SMEARS to EM...RASS and 'involved in' places BAR within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to show them up, causing awkward shame.

clue.text: Ruin game with sporting bloomer

indicators.note: sporting means playful or frolicking, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Spoil a match with a fair-minded blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A geranium is a flowering plant, something that blooms.

clue.text: Measure of wind: good and strong off Brittany, given by a number of notes

parts.note: beau is French for fine or good, French being signalled by off Brittany
fort is French for strong
a scale is a series of musical notes

explanation.surface: Weather report: fine and blustery off the Breton coast, measured in musical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off Brittany' tells you to use French words: BEAU (good) and FORT (strong). Then add SCALE, a run of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort scale grades wind force from calm to hurricane on a numbered table.

clue.text: Some member in favour, given attention by one-third of MPs

parts.note: for means in favour
to give ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: one-third of a three-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Part of the house votes yes, heeded by a third of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests an MP; it is a limb. MPs has three letters, so one third is M.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm is part of the arm, a body limb.

clue.text: Radical relaxes, wasting time for vengeance

parts.note: a red is a radical left-winger

indicators.note: wasting says a letter is lost from the word

parts.note: rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: An extremist takes it easy, frittering time away, in pursuit of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' takes the T out of RESTS to leave RESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is putting a wrong right, as in seeking retribution.

clue.text: Film line: namely a grave comment before end of shot

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, meaning namely
RIP, rest in peace, is the comment on a gravestone

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Words for a movie: specifically a solemn remark ahead of the final take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like serious; it is a tombstone, inscribed RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a film's lines.

clue.text: Someone with a disease- Published by Independent&news Media Limited passenger, say, dropping dead

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall from the longer phrase

parts.note: a passenger in a car is, for example, a car rider

explanation.surface: An infected person, perhaps a passenger, losing a life.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has the paper's imprint line 'Published by Independent&news Media Limited' run into it by the page layout; those words play no part. CAR RIDER loses its D for CARRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier harbours an infection and can pass it on, often without symptoms.

clue.text: Quantity of water from inactive main?

parts.note: something dead is inactive or inert
the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Water drawn from a disused supply pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like a water main; it is the sea, as in 'the Spanish Main'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, a body of water.

clue.text: US typist not entirely fast enough

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, the run inside it

explanation.surface: An American secretary not quite quick enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across faST ENOugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Steno is American shorthand for a stenographer.

clue.text: Stupid wanting to hold one carpet still

indicators.note: wanting to hold says the word for stupid takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: inane means silly or stupid
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A dim person keen to grab a single rug that stays motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' looks like a verb meaning scold; it is a MAT. INANE holds I + MAT: INAN-IMAT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate is lifeless and motionless.

clue.text: Tribe held back in reserve, at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for reserve comes at the front

parts.note: ice means cool reserve, a frosty manner

indicators.note: held back says the little word in is turned round

explanation.surface: A tribe kept back in the reserve land at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns IN into NI, and 'at first' puts ICE (reserve, coolness of manner) before it. The Iceni were the British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British people of East Anglia.

clue.text: Closed and quiet? Nonsense

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Shut up and be silent? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: TO means closed, as in 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Give wrong data to girl mostly working well

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
in form means performing well

explanation.surface: Mislead a young woman who is mostly doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MISS to MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to feed someone false facts.
